variants.name: suspend/CPS: compiler-generated Continuation
variants.implementation_notes: Kotlin's suspend keyword is the token: the compiler transforms every suspend function into continuation-passing style (a state machine taking a Continuation<T>), and the completing side resumes exactly that continuation through resumeWith (or the resume/resumeWithException extensions), so the demultiplexing is done by the compiler and the coroutine machinery - no token table and no lookup by request id. kotlinx.coroutines supplies the builders and dispatchers (async/await, withContext, Deferred.await); where an external API completes through a callback, suspendCancellableCoroutine exposes the CancellableContinuation that becomes the explicit token for that bridge.
pitfalls: Prompt cancellation guarantee: a successful resume racing with cancellation of the job is discarded and its value dropped - if it carries a closeable resource, release it through invokeOnCancellation or the resume(value) { onCancellation } overload.

The register/unregister bodies of suspendCancellableCoroutine run on arbitrary threads: invokeOnCancellation can run concurrently with the completing callback, so shared state needs its own synchronisation.
A custom ContinuationInterceptor that does not extend CoroutineDispatcher voids the prompt cancellation guarantee, leaving a cancelled operation unable to notice.

variants.name: CompletableDeferred as an explicit token object
variants.implementation_notes: Where the completion is not a single await - an operation completed by an external event, observed by several coroutines, or kept as a handle - CompletableDeferred is the classic ACT as an object: the client holds the Deferred, the completing side calls complete/completeExceptionally once, and any number of coroutines await it (or attach onAwait). It is the right shape at interop edges (a callback library, a message arriving on a channel) and when the registry that maps request ids to tokens has to be explicit.
variants.code_sketch:
val pending = ConcurrentHashMap<RequestId, CompletableDeferred<Reply>>()
val token = CompletableDeferred<Reply>()          // explicit ACT
pending[request.id] = token
onReply { id, reply -> pending.remove(id)?.complete(reply) }
val reply = token.await()
pitfalls: complete() returns false when the deferred is already complete or cancelled, and a cancelled deferred counts as complete - a racing loser is silently ignored unless you inspect the result and use completeExceptionally for failures.
Keeping deferreds in a registry retains the coroutines awaiting them; remove entries on completion, timeout and cancellation.
